Inspired by traditional forums, I think the ability to move discussion from one verse to another would make the site more versatile.

Say someone makes a non-question in /v/AskVoat, rather than deleting the thread I could move it to /v/Voat. This would retain the author's original message and all the comment that were made.

How could this be implemented? I think a move next to the delete, flair, toggle, sticky would be easy enough. When clicked, a textbox appears below asking which subverse to put the discussion/link. Maybe an auto-PM notification could tell the author that the discussion got moved.

I was thinking that there should also be a moderator approval process before the content shows up on the new subverse, but this may not be the most convenient process. Perhaps a subverse setting could toggle an auto-approval versus moderator approval.

Interesting idea! This might cut down on having to remove posts that really belong in another subverse.

My only suggestion would be for an automatic reinstatement of the post in the originating sub if the moderator of the target sub doesn't approve it after a certain amount of time. That way posts don't get stuck in limbo.

Hi all,

Apologies if this is a silly question to be asking here, but I'd thought it's worth a shot (no pun intended!) to get more experienced photographers thoughts on a problem I'm having.

I'm relatively new to photography and I recently got a new camera that I've fallen in love with - Olympus OMD EM10. Although leaving it on Auto or using the presets is tempting, I want to get the most out the camera and actually learn all the features. Yesterday I took it out to a sculpture park to experiment with shots as there's lots of opportunity with the landscape, sculptures, building, people etc.

The issue I'm having is with manual focus. When looking through my viewfinder, and changing it to what I consider to be in complete focus I later found out that I was wrong. The results varied so widely which is why I'm confused. Some are crisp and exactly how I saw them through my viewfinder, and some (particularly with portrait shots) came out blurry. I wasn't using a tripod just in case that's relevant.

Is there a reason for this? To me, it looked like they were in focus but obviously the pictures differ. It's probably a silly mistake I'm making but I would really appreciate any suggestions!

I have had a similar problem with a different camera, a Pentax K01. The problem is not the camera or the lens, but camera shake, not focus [as much].

Definitely a different situation, my cam is mirrorless and doesn't have a viewfinder (which increases my issue with stability) but you might want to consider that, especially if you're talking about low light and no tripod. Got any samples?

As I've heard said before, digital systems are not really designed for manual focus. I shoot manually 99% of the time on my D3100 as a secondary. And many many times what I think is in focus is not what the camera thinks is, on Nikons there is a little circle that displays when focus is correct, if I don't see that I defer to the system and adjust accordingly. Doing that I don't have a big problem with out of focus images. So look for a 'focus indicator' setting or whatever it us on your system. It's a huge help!
